record.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Wonder Full with a 1M-token context and broad agent evaluations
record.summary: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on October 12, 2026. Its research post describes both as models for personal and professional agent tasks, while the linked model card lists a 1M-token inference context and evaluations spanning agent work, coding, and general capability. The models are available through Meta's API and Muse Code, with Wonder Full limited to Muse Code subscribers. Meta reports state-of-the-art benchmark performance, but the model card says it selects the highest available result where comparable results differ and that its internally run comparisons against proprietary competitors are best-effort. This is evidence of a substantial model release and of Meta's reported evaluation, not independent confirmation of broad capability leadership; a fuller safety report is still forthcoming.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Meta's October 12, 2026 research post and newsroom announcement introduce Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full; the post says Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code and Wonder Full for Muse Code subscribers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Meta's model card lists a 1M-token inference context and reports evaluations across agent, coding, and general-capability tasks; these are provider-reported specifications and evaluations, not independently reproduced here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Meta describes the models as state of the art across selected benchmarks, but its card says it may use the highest of internal, self-reported, or leaderboard scores and that proprietary competitor runs are best-effort, with prompts, tools, and runtime potentially not optimally tuned.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched evaluation of Muse Wonder and Wonder Full across the provider-highlighted agent and coding tasks was located in this recent-window check.
Meta states that additional safety evaluations will be published in a forthcoming full report; that report was not available in the inspected announcement/model card.
No comparable price, latency, throughput or workload-level cost data were inspected for either model.

brief.importance_rationale: If the release's reported agent and coding performance generalizes, it marks Meta's return to frontier model competition and supplies two commercially available models with 1M-token inference context, potentially shifting model choice and agent-platform competition. Score 5 reflects broad industry and deployment relevance; performance leadership is not independently established.
limitations: Benchmark leadership is Meta-reported and was not independently reproduced in this activation.
The model card says it selects the highest of internally validated, self-reported or official leaderboard scores where comparable results exist, which can favor peak over typical results.
Internally generated competitor results are best-effort; Meta states prompts, tools and runtime may not be optimally tuned for proprietary models.
The release's Active Memory and Active Focus descriptions do not establish real-world reliability or performance across independent agent tasks.
Meta says a full report with additional safety evaluations will be published later; the public evidence inspected here is incomplete for safety evaluation.
Training compute, energy use and comparable inference economics are not reported in the inspected sources.

technical.claimed_result: Meta reports state-of-the-art results on selected agent, memory and coding benchmarks and lists a 1M-token inference context.
technical.compute_or_cost: The announcement identifies Meta's gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center as a training site but provides no training-compute accounting or comparable inference cost in the inspected material.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated public release, stated access channels and published model-card contents are directly observable. Comparative capability claims remain provider-reported.
technical.implementation_status: Muse Wonder is listed as available through Meta Model API and Muse Code; Wonder Full is listed for Muse Code subscribers. Availability was not independently tested.
technical.mechanism: Meta positions Muse Wonder and Wonder Full as models built across pretraining and reinforcement learning for persistent agent tasks, with described Active Memory and Active Focus behaviors. Public materials inspected do not disclose enough training detail to independently assess the mechanism.
technical.regime: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, max reasoning effort in the model card's evaluations; comparisons include GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5, with a mixture of internal, provider and third-party results.
technical.reproducibility: No independent reproduction or model access test was performed. The model card identifies internal and third-party evaluation sources but no general release of evaluation code/data was established in this review.
technical.strongest_baseline: The model card compares several named frontier systems, but per-benchmark sources and harnesses vary; its general methodology says proprietary competitors may not be optimally tuned.

brief.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Wonder Full with a 1M-token context and broad agent evaluations
brief.why_it_matters: The launch combines a new frontier-positioned model family, long inference context, and deployment through API and coding tools, making Meta a consequential option in the agent-model market. The disclosed evaluation caveats matter: comparisons mix internal and external results, competitor settings may be untuned, and some headline framing is Meta's own. Independent evaluation and the promised safety report will determine how much of the claimed breadth transfers beyond the company's measured setup.
